suggestions.quote: At the 1992 Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver (c08). Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing (c08).
suggestions.fix: At the 1992 Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver medallists (c08). Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of finishing without a medal (c08).

suggestions.quote: The exam grades on a curve. In most subjects, only the top 4 per cent get the top grade (c01).
suggestions.fix: The national exam grades on a curve. In most subjects, only the top 4 per cent get the top grade (c01).

keep.quote: In one brain-scan study, envying a peer who did better at something that mattered came with activity in a region also active in pain (c05).

Here's what you had backwards. You treated the four per cent like four places in a room. But in most subjects, it's the top 4 per cent of everyone in the country who sat it (c01). His grade never cost you yours.
Envy comes in two kinds (c07). One pushes you to move up. The other pushes you to pull the other person down (c07).
